title: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome
diseaseDescription: Bounded complement-mediated aHUS: inherited or acquired complement dysregulation at endothelial surfaces, terminal complement injury and thrombotic microangiopathy. Human cohorts, endothelial assays and animal experiments remain distinct. Excludes STEC-HUS, TTP, secondary TMA, DGKE and cobalamin-related TMA. Selected genetic, antibody, endothelial-assay and terminal-pathway studies only. Factor B, THBD, triggers and full clinical manifestation sequence remain deferred rather than inferred.
releaseNote: Provisional automatic appraisal of atypical-hus-candidate-contexts-20261017-02. Automatic conservative metadata appraisal. Source entailment, study quality, broad disease coverage, circuit causation and independent replication require review. Confidence is capped at 1/4 until explicit editorial appraisal; therapeutic categories describe curated target coverage, not efficacy. No calibration or human approval is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

entities.label: Complement-regulatory gene variants
entities.description: Selected CFH, CFI and CD46 susceptibility variants; variant-specific functional evidence and incomplete penetrance are retained.

entities.label: Factor H regulatory activity
entities.description: Surface recognition and complement regulation; patient autoantibody binding and inhibition are studied in biochemical assays.

entities.label: Anti-factor H autoantibodies
entities.description: Patient antibodies to factor H; studied C-terminal binding inhibits surface recognition.

entities.label: CFHR1/CFHR3 deficiency
entities.description: Inherited deficiency associated with anti-factor H autoantibodies in a selected cohort; not sufficient by itself to establish disease.

entities.label: Factor I regulatory activity
entities.description: Complement protease activity; selected CFI variants impair secretion or surface C3b cleavage.

entities.label: CD46 surface regulation
entities.description: Membrane cofactor protein function; R69W/A304V cell challenge experiments retain variant and model limits.

entities.label: C3 susceptibility variants
entities.description: Selected C3 variants in a low-C3 patient series; both gain-of-function and inactivating variants were reported.

entities.label: Alternative complement pathway dysregulation
entities.description: Failure to regulate alternative complement activity; fluid phase and endothelial-surface readouts are distinct.

entities.label: aHUS patient serum
entities.description: Patient serum sampled during acute disease or remission, tested on human endothelial cells.

entities.label: Endothelial C5b-9 deposition
entities.description: Terminal complement membrane attack complex on endothelial surfaces; assay readout is not equivalent to clinical disease.

entities.label: C5a–C5aR1 signalling
entities.description: Terminal complement inflammatory signalling, genetically and pharmacologically perturbed in distinct mouse models.

entities.label: Renal thrombotic microangiopathy
entities.description: Renal small-vessel pathology in mouse experiments; human trial outcomes use their specified TMA definitions.

entities.label: Macrovascular thrombosis
entities.description: Separate outcome in factor H mutant mice; not substituted for renal TMA or universal human disease.

entities.label: aHUS susceptibility / penetrance
entities.description: Human genetic association and incomplete penetrance; not a deterministic genotype-to-disease pathway.

entities.label: Eculizumab exposure
entities.description: C5 inhibitor exposure in endothelial assays and separate uncontrolled clinical trials.

entities.label: Clinical TMA response
entities.description: Trial-specific platelet and TMA event-free outcomes; not identical across studies.

entities.label: Loss of kidney function
entities.description: Renal impairment or recovery endpoints in selected aHUS trials; reversal is not assured.

entities.label: Complement C5 cleavage
entities.description: Terminal complement target; cleavage generates C5a and C5b, with subsequent MAC formation.
